section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch10 — Memory — Deep Practice
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Remembering how to ride a bicycle, without consciously recalling step-by-step verbal instructions, is an example of:
explanation: Procedural memory stores skills/how-to knowledge (riding a bike), often without conscious verbal recall. Episodic memory is for personal events; semantic memory is for facts/general knowledge.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch10 — Memory — Deep Practice
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Remembering the capital of France (Paris) is an example of:
explanation: Semantic memory stores general facts/knowledge (like capital cities), independent of when/where you learned it. Episodic memory stores personally experienced events.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch11 — Personality — Deep Practice
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Carl Jung's distinction between individuals who draw energy from social interaction versus those who draw energy from solitary reflection is the:
explanation: Jung's extraversion-introversion distinction concerns where a person draws psychological energy from — social engagement (extraversion) versus internal reflection (introversion) — later incorporated into trait models like the Big Five.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch11 — Personality — Deep Practice
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student who fails an exam and immediately claims 'the test was unfair anyway, I didn't even want to do well' is displaying which Freudian defense mechanism?
explanation: Rationalisation involves creating a plausible but false justification to avoid facing an uncomfortable truth (failure). Repression pushes distressing thoughts out of awareness; projection attributes one's own unwanted feelings to others.
